title: Part Two, Chapter 10: The Houses of Cold, Jaguars, Fire and Bats

verses.t: And they entered the house of cold. The cold in it was unbearable, and so was the ice that was in it, in the house of cold; and then the cold was ended by them, the young men, and they did not die, but dawned alive. And this was what those of the underworld wanted: to see them die, and that they should die there; but it was not so. Rather they were well when dawn came. And those who came to call them were watching closely, and the guards went away, and the lord of the underworld said, "What is this? How is it they have not died?" And they marvelled again at the wonders of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque. And then they entered the house of jaguars; those in that house could not be counted. "Do not bite us," they said to them. "Here, let this be your food!" And then they threw bones before the beasts, and then these began to crunch the bones. "There, they are finished; they have been eaten; they have given in. Those are their bones, what they are eating." This is what all the guards said, and they were glad of it. But they did not die, and so they came out well from the house of jaguars; and those of the underworld said, "What kind of men are you? Where have you come from?"

And then they put them into a house of fire, where there was nothing but fire; and they were not burned by the fire, but were handsome and well when dawn came. And what they wanted was that they should die there at once, within the fire; but they overcame this as well, and at that those of the underworld were in despair.

And then, once more, into the house of bats, where there was nothing inside but bats, a house of bats, great seizing brutes like Chaquitzam, which was their killer, for those who came before them perished at once. And they stayed inside there, but they slept inside their blowguns and were not bitten by the bats; and there they stayed, because of a great bat that came from the sky and showed itself when it was made by him; and they took counsel. All night the bats were whirling about and saying, "Quilitz! Quilitz!" So they kept saying all night; and when they all stopped, not one of the bats was moving any more; they clung to the end of the blowgun. And Xbalanque said to Hun-ahpu, "Perhaps it has dawned by now; let us see!" And wanting to see, Hun-ahpu put his head out at the mouth of the blowgun; he wanted to see whether it had dawned. And at once his head was cut off by Camazotz, and only Hun-ahpu's body was left. The other, Xbalanque, said, "Has it dawned?" But Hun-ahpu did not move. "What has happened? Can Hun-ahpu have gone? How did this happen?" And he no longer moved, but lay stretched out. And then Xbalanque was frightened: "Alas, alas, unhappy one!" This is what he said. And then they went and put the head in the ball court, for so Hun-came and Vucub-came had ordered; and all those of the underworld rejoiced over the head of Hun-ahpu.
